newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel offered lower, Russian pressed.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel offered lower, Russian pressed.

text.p: Euro low sulphur straight-run was steady to lower on softer crude prices while Russian high sulphur material continues to face some downward pressure from high supply and little demand.

Traders said one seller of low sulphur straight-run was offering at $109/$110 fob but buyers were $2 to $3 lower, while a second seller said he was at $113, some $2 lower than his asking price on Friday.
"With crude lower we cut the price a bit," the seller, a refiner, said.
"There's still a standoff in the market between sellers and buyers at $109 and $106/$107," a second seller said.

Russian high sulphur straight-run, especially E-4, continued to be distressed from increasing exports in the second half of August, and little demand, with refiners sticking to buying crude instead of feedstocks.

E-4 was bid at three means-$2/$1 and offered at flat, while traders were mixed about M-100 values, with some putting them at two means +$3.50 for offers with bids at $2.30 over the quote and others saying it was lower.
"M-100 varies according to grade and quality but it is getting on the verge of flowing into the cracked market," one seller said.
Three M-100 cargoes and a similar number of E-4s were looking for homes, as the Russians began to export more after straight-run premiums rose a few weeks earlier.
With a wide barge-cargo differential and with straight-run seeking outlets, one M-100 cargo was heard placed late last week in the bunker blending market, which has risen to high levels recently.
"With Iraq back on the market, crude price went down and so people are buying less feedstocks and every one is waiting for prices to come down," a second trader said.

"There were also a lot of deals in August and many people are covered while Russian exports in the second half of July are rising. The Russians reacted to the higher straight-run prices earlier by starting to export more. So there's a double effect there," he added.
